title: Run journal line (gtm/runs/{run-id}.jsonl)
description: One line per row per hop. Written BEFORE and AFTER each call so a kill mid-call is recoverable. Substrate for --dry-run (all rows pending, zero calls), resume, the share-safe aggregate render, and /learn's provider hit-rates.

row_id.description: stable per input row; the resume key

status.description: skipped_cache = read-through cache hit, not charged. skipped_suppressed = fail-closed suppression drop.

credits_actual.description: null when the response carries no billing field — see ledger cost_status

response_hash.description: sha256 of the response body; row-level data itself is NOT stored here

provider.description: email_finder returns this; the input to /learn's per-segment hit-rate memory

error.description: Short machine code only (e.g. `http.429`, `provider.no_match`). The pattern is the point: a free-text error is the easiest way for a contact to leak into the journal, e.g. "no result for ada@example.com".

attempt.description: 429 Retry-After discipline; a retried row must not double-charge the ledger

dry_run.description: True for a line written by --dry-run: planned, never attempted, zero calls made. Without this a dry-run row is indistinguishable from a row killed mid-call, so resume would treat every planned row as a possible double-charge.

list_key.description: Identifies the input list this run covers. Needed so /comply erase and the TTL sweep can find a run's sidecar concurrency lock (gtm/runs/.locks/*.lock), which otherwise no contract covers.

$comment: PII rule: this file carries row_id and response_hash, never contact fields. The shareable dry-run render is aggregate-only BY CONSTRUCTION and has a PII-strip regression test.
